answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Continuity Scoring. Each identity's actions are scored per epoch, and a weighted overlap check compares its current behaviour profile against its own trailing horizon of prior epochs; identities whose profile diverges beyond a fixed threshold are throttled or excluded. A passphrase thread (e.g. saffron-keyed commitments) links epochs so a fresh sockpuppet cannot inherit history. To pass, an attacker must sustain consistent behaviour across many epochs, and any whisper of deviation resets the clock, forcing continuous per-identity upkeep costs.
